system.name: OctoSketch
system.one_liner: a system enabling real-time, continuous network monitoring over multiple CPU cores

content.key_idea: Driver, application, and monitoring code all compete for the same per-core CPU resources once the NIC spreads traffic across cores, so per-core monitoring results must then be aggregated globally.
content.reading_order: Top to bottom: traffic enters the NIC and fans into three identical core columns, each stacking Driver, Application, and Monitoring, collected on the left by the Aggregator.

Figure 1 shows a typical workflow for monitoring traffic distributed over multiple cores

summary: Figure 1 illustrates the motivating multicore monitoring problem that OctoSketch addresses. Incoming traffic arrives at a NIC, which distributes packets into multiple Rx queues; three CPU cores (Core 1, Core 2, Core 3) each poll one or more of these queues through a Driver (e.g., DPDK PMD). On every core, the polled packets are then handed to an Application (e.g., a load balancer) and, in parallel, to a Monitoring program, both of which compete with the driver for the same per-core CPU resources. Each core's Monitoring output is collected by a single Aggregator on the left, which must combine per-core statistics into a global, timely measurement result. The figure is drawn as a grid with Driver, Application, and Monitoring as three identically colored horizontal bands repeated across the three core columns, emphasizing the shared-resource and aggregation challenges of monitoring at multicore scale.
summary_zh: 图1展示OctoSketch面对的多核监控问题：NIC将流量分发到多个Rx队列，三个CPU核各自通过驱动轮询并运行应用与监控程序，三者共享同一核资源；各核监控结果再由左侧Aggregator聚合，构成典型的多核监控工作流。
